title: Sixth pillar of Iman – belief in qadar
intro: Everything that happens – good and bad – happens by Allah’s will and decree.

learn.label: The sixth pillar of Iman
learn.ar: وَبِالْقَدَرِ خَيْرِهِ وَشَرِّهِ مِنَ اللَّهِ تَعَالَى
learn.tr: Wa bil-qadari khayrihi wa sharrihi minallaahi ta‘aalaa
learn.en: And (I believe) that everything that happens, good and bad, happens by Allah’s will and decree.

learn.html: This is how we understand Allah’s will and decree: Allah (SWT) is the Creator of everything. He decides how, when, where and what will happen. What Allah wills, happens; what He does not will, cannot happen.

learn.text: When we say we believe in qadar, we believe:

items: that everything was written long ago in the Lawh al-Mahfuz,
that nothing happens without Allah’s knowledge, and

learn.html: In the Lawh al-Mahfuz – the Preserved Tablet – everything that happens in the heavens and on Earth is written. The destiny of every person is written there too, and everything else that can affect it. Nothing can happen that is not written.

learn.title: Hadith
learn.html: The Prophet (SAW) said: “You will not taste the sweetness of Iman until you believe that whatever has reached you could not have missed you, and whatever has missed you could not have reached you.” <small>(Muslim)</small>

learn.text: What is decided for us, and what we choose

learn.html: Before a person is born, it is decided when and where they will be born, who their parents will be, whether they will be a boy or a girl, what their life will be like, what their provision (rizq) will be, and when and where they will die. A person is not responsible for these things.

A person is responsible only for the deeds they choose. They are completely free to choose whether to live by Allah’s rules or not, whether to carry out their Islamic duties or not, and whether to do good or evil. Because of this free will, a person is responsible for their deeds – in this world and in the next.

learn.title: ⭐ Remember
learn.html: We know what we have been commanded, but we do not know what has been decreed – so we should act on what we have been commanded.

practice.title: Decided for us, or our choice?
practice.prompt: Is it decided for us before we are born, or is it our own choice?
